decision.summary: The Fed raised its policy rate by 75 basis points, to 3% to 3.25%. The vote was 12-0.

changes.quote: Recent indicators point to modest growth in spending and production.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Recent indicators of spending and production have softened.”

changes.quote: Job gains have been robust in recent months, and the unemployment rate has remained low.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Nonetheless, job gains have been robust in recent months, and the unemployment rate has remained low.”

changes.quote: In support of these goals, the Committee decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate to 3 to 3-1/4 percent and anticipates that ongoing increases in the target range will be appropriate.

tone_quotes.quote: In support of these goals, the Committee decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate to 3 to 3-1/4 percent and anticipates that ongoing increases in the target range will be appropriate.
Inflation remains elevated, reflecting supply and demand imbalances related to the pandemic, higher food and energy prices, and broader price pressures.
The Committee is strongly committed to returning inflation to its 2 percent objective.

for_you.text: On a $5,000 card balance at about 15.13% APR, a 75 bp increase raises monthly interest by about $3.13.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 3.51% and moved -6 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 5.89% would fall by about $11.50 a month.
High-yield savings rates usually follow the Fed partly; on $10,000 that means roughly $45.00 a year more in interest.
Unemployment was 3.6%, and employers added an average of 479k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 8.2% over the past year (August 2022); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 5.4%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 0.6% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved +6 bp on the day, and the S&P 500 moved -1.71%.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved 0.49% on the day.

whats_next: The dictionary tone reading is hawkish (leaning toward higher rates). The forecast model gave the next meeting: hold 0%, cut 0%, hike 100%.
